name: octoprint
summary: 3D printer management platform for remote control, monitoring, job execution, and print workflow automation.
why_it_matters: OctoPrint captures useful additive-manufacturing capability knowledge, but hardware coupling and no current usage make it a blueprint rather than a supported resource.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs remote 3D printer management.
Operators want print job orchestration, monitoring, or webcam integration.
The workflow depends on existing OctoPrint APIs and plugins.

platform_support.notes: The application can run in containers, but useful operation depends on host access to printer hardware and related peripherals.

implementation_notes: Promotion should target one or two validated printer workflows.
Keep hardware control boundaries explicit and safety-aware.
Plugin usage should be constrained rather than open-ended.
operational_notes: Serial access and hardware permissions are the main portability issue.
Validation should prove job upload and printer communication.
Print artifacts and timelapses need explicit retention rules.
risks: Hardware-adjacent automation can create real operational failures.
A generic wrapper would overpromise portability and support.
